editorial:
Imagine your entire world crashing down in one single second. That is exactly what happens to Allison, a young woman who gets into a terrible car accident that changes everything. You will feel for her as she deals with massive guilt and a life that feels totally broken. The story gets interesting when she starts spending time with her would-be father-in-law. They are both hurting in their own ways, and seeing these two strangers bond over their shared pain feels very real and touching. It is a slow burn that focuses more on feelings and conversations than big action scenes, making it feel like a quiet, intimate look at how people heal.

Florence Pugh is amazing here and really carries the emotional weight of the film. You might find the pacing a bit slow at times, but the honest acting makes it work. If you enjoy stories about forgiveness and second chances, you should definitely give this one a try. For the best experience, you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the beautiful scenery, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this emotional journey on your shelf.
endingExplained: By the end, Allison finally stops running from her guilt. She accepts that she cannot change the past but can choose to be a better person now. She and the father-in-law find a way to move forward together, showing that love and friendship can grow from the worst tragedies. It wraps up on a hopeful note, leaving you feeling that healing is possible if you let people in and forgive yourself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories about forgiveness and human connection.
